subject.title: [Bug]: Discord sessions persist per-session exec directives, causing allowlist mode to behave unexpectedly after config changes

question: Should later operator `tools.exec.*` config hardening override persisted per-session `/exec` values for existing Discord sessions, and how should existing stored entries be reset or migrated?
rationale: Current source and docs intentionally persist authorized `/exec` session defaults, but the reported failure affects exec security policy enforcement after config changes, so automation should not choose the security boundary alone.

options.title: Make operator security config dominant
options.body: Change precedence or invalidation so stricter `tools.exec.*` changes take effect for existing sessions, with focused tests and doctor/reset handling for stored exec fields.

options.title: Keep per-session `/exec` persistence
options.body: Treat current behavior as intentional and improve diagnostics/docs so operators know to inspect or clear per-session overrides separately.

options.title: Add explicit reset without precedence change
options.body: Preserve current precedence but add an operator-facing way to clear exec overrides across affected sessions after config changes.

recommendation.title: Make operator security config dominant
recommendation.body: Change precedence or invalidation so stricter `tools.exec.*` changes take effect for existing sessions, with focused tests and doctor/reset handling for stored exec fields.

likelyOwner.reason: He authored the original `/exec` session override behavior and the focused resolver coverage that now encodes the precedence contract.
